Free Printable Itch Diary (PDF) — Eczema Itch & Scratch Log

This is a free, one-page printable itch diary in PDF format. Each row is one itch episode or one time slot: the date, time of day, itch intensity from 0 to 10, where on the body, whether you scratched and how much sleep it cost, and what was happening at the time — heat, sweat, fabric, a bath, stress. Flare trackers record the skin; this sheet records the symptom that actually disrupts your day and night, which is the thing a dermatologist most often asks about and the thing patients find hardest to describe from memory. It is a record-keeping aid, not medical advice.

Why log itch separately from flares

Visible eczema and itch do not always move together. Itch often spikes in the evening and at night, after exercise, or during stressful weeks, while the skin looks the same. A diary that only records how the skin looked misses the pattern. Scoring itch on a simple 0–10 scale at a few fixed points — morning, afternoon, evening, night — turns 'it has been bad lately' into a line your dermatologist can read, and shows whether a change in routine actually helped.

Record the context without judging it. 'Wool sweater', 'hot shower', 'gym', 'deadline', 'new detergent' are observations. Over two or three weeks, the ones that keep appearing beside high scores are worth discussing with your clinician; the sheet does not decide what they mean.

Scoring and what to note

Anchors for the 0–10 column, and the context most people find worth writing down. Use whatever words fit — consistency matters more than the exact number.

ScoreWhat it feels likeContext worth noting
0No itch—
1–3Noticeable but easy to ignore; no scratching neededTime of day, what you were wearing
4–6Hard to ignore; you scratch or rub, can still concentrateHeat, sweat, fabric, bathing, a new product
7–9Dominates attention; scratching is hard to stop; disturbs sleepStress, illness, missed routine, sleep lost (hours)
10Worst imaginable; cannot sleep or functionEverything above — and tell your clinician

Scales like this are commonly used in dermatology for patient-reported itch; your clinician may prefer a specific one. The sheet works with any of them.

How to use this sheet

  1. Print the PDF and keep it by the bed — night is when itch is usually worst and least remembered.
  2. Score itch 0–10 at fixed points (morning, afternoon, evening, bedtime) and whenever an episode stands out.
  3. Note where on the body it was and whether you scratched, and estimate sleep lost in hours.
  4. In What was happening, write the plain facts: heat, sweat, wool, hot shower, stress, new detergent, missed moisturizer.
  5. After two to three weeks, bring the sheets to your dermatologist appointment.

Questions

Is this sheet really free?

Yes. The PDF is free to download and print — no sign-up, no email, no watermark.

Is this a medical form?

No. It is a personal record sheet to help you describe symptoms accurately. It does not diagnose, and it does not replace advice from a dermatologist or doctor.

How often should I fill it in?

A few fixed times a day works better than 'whenever it itches', because it captures the quiet days too. Add extra rows for episodes that stand out.

Should I log itch if my skin looks clear?

Yes — that is one of the most useful things the sheet records. Itch without visible flare is common and worth telling your clinician about.
